 POST HEARING BRIEF OF PRO-SE INTERVENOR TRACY SNELL MACK (TTEE)
         OF THE M.A. SNELL INVESTMENTS TRUST (PARTY #819)


        I, Tracy Snell Mack, TTEE on behalf of the M. A. Snell Investments Trust, pro se
intervenor #819, submit this initial Post-Hearing Brief respectfully requesting that the ALJ’s
deny the project in its entirety for the reasons described below, and if unable to deny the project
entirely, I strongly request to refuse any routes that include Link U1 or G52.
                                           INTRODUCTION
         Our family has continuously ranched and stewarded this property (Tract #5056, 5056.9)
through multi-generations since 1901. The property is currently used as a primary homestead and
for raising cattle with a goal to continue preserving the land and its ecological heritage for
wildlife, hunting, fishing, ranching and recreation for many generations to follow.
        While our initial concerns revolved around environmental and aesthetic disruption, the
further along the intervenor process we have come, another primary concern is general
landowner rights and the lack of integrity this process has revealed- especially in regards to pro-
se intervenor / landowners.
                             THE PROCESS AS A PRO-SE INTERVENOR
        As a landowner affected by an alternate route (Link U1) that was added later in the
process, we did not receive formal notice from the applicants until almost mid-April 2026 with
an initial deadline of April 27th to file protest and intervenor forms. Less than two weeks were
given for landowners on our link to try and understand what was going on and how we could
attempt to participate in a meaningful way. Our first thought was to contact an attorney but due
to our link being added later in the process, majority of any relevant attorney’s had already been
acquired by other landowners and therefore they were unable to help due to conflict of interest
(landowners on other routes).

       Next, we decided to contact and coordinate with other landowners on the U1 link which
we found by cross referencing the applicants provided map and landowner tract #s with the
Lampasas CAD in which we were able to identify and come in to contact with the majority of
landowners on our segment. As expected, most of the U1 landowners were also unsure where to
begin and unable to obtain representation for guidance due to the lack of availability. In an
attempt to “come together” we filed a joint-landowner protest opposing any routes that include
link U1. The participating opposing landowners own a combined 3,7609 + acres of the link U1
segment.
        Fortunately, there have been a handful of more experienced landowners and concerned
citizens that have provided guidance and direction in the process thus far to the general
public/pro-se intervenors via social media. The lack of guidance from either of the applicants has
made a highly technical process seem nearly impossible to navigate without prior experience
and/or formal representation leaving the average landowner to fend for themselves, and their
properties on their own.

        As an inexperienced pro-se intervenor who naively expected to have an opportunity to
speak up during the hearing of the merits and later learned we would not have this opportunity, it
feels necessary to bring some of these issues from the process to your attention from an average
participants perspective.
         The lack of coordination and inorganization by the applicants has been evident from the
start of this process. The hearing itself was chaotic and complicated from all of the time spent on
clerical issues, updates, and corrections, etc. We experienced this personally despite submitting
all of our exhibits on time to each of the three platforms required by Oncor/LCRA with less than
a couple of days notice to do so, it still took until Thursday (Day 4 of hearing) for our exhibits to
be accepted.
                                        IN CONCLUSION
       Considering the complexity of this project, the process, and a full week of trial without
any persuasion from the applicant’s side regarding the necessity of this project, we strongly
agree with the American Stewards of Liberty’s motion to defer determination of need.
       Alternative and less destructive options may be available and should be considered; such
as generating power directly from the Permian Basin. I am requesting all regulatory affiliates to
conduct full extensive review, analysis and studies on the entire route and overall cause of
necessity for this project and that all findings be meticulously considered and presented before
proceeding with any decision.
       There are irreplaceable legacy ranches that have protected their properties for decades
and even centuries and to subject these landowners to a 180-day ruling seems unjust, unethical,
and un-Texan without considering all possible alternatives. We plea with you to pause and
reconsider.


                                                                          Respectfully Submitted,
                                                                         Tracy Snell Mack

                                                                          Tracy Snell Mack TTEE

                                                                    M.A. Snell Investments Trust
